Drug properties affecting response: 5

A patient takes an oral antibiotic with an iron supplement, forming poorly absorbed complexes in the bowel. Which drug-interaction mechanism explains reduced exposure without requiring a change in liver metabolism or renal elimination?

  1. Additive pharmacodynamic effects
  2. Complex formation reducing absorption
  3. Lipid solubility and membrane passage
  4. Molecular size limiting passive membrane passage
  5. Formulation-dependent release
Answer and explanation

Complex formation reducing absorption

Binding of some medicines to polyvalent cations can reduce gastrointestinal absorption.

Option explanations

Complex formation reducing absorption: Binding of some medicines to polyvalent cations can reduce gastrointestinal absorption.

Lipid solubility and membrane passage: Physicochemical properties influence membrane penetration, distribution and sometimes CNS entry. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Molecular size limiting passive membrane passage: Large molecules often cross lipid membranes poorly without specialized transport or delivery. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Formulation-dependent release: Immediate- and modified-release products can have different concentration-time profiles despite containing the same drug. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Additive pharmacodynamic effects: Two medicines with similar physiological actions can increase the combined effect or toxicity. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
